neighbours.label: an attributive severity adjective framing an unpleasant truth (the harsh reality, the stark truth, the brutal realities), predicting 'reality'; as opposed to neutral framings of the same facts
fire: The film confronts viewers with the harsh realities of addiction.
Farmers now face the harsh truth that the rains may not return.
The report exposes the stark reality of child poverty in the region.
Young athletes soon learn the harsh lessons of professional sport.
The memoir describes the brutal realities of life on the front line.
Parents must explain the harsh facts of the illness to their children.
The data reveal the stark truth about how little workers are paid.
Many graduates are meeting the harsh reality of a weak job market.
quiet: The film confronts viewers with the daily routines of addiction recovery.
Farmers now face the simple fact that the rains may return late.
The report examines the current state of child care in the region.
Young athletes soon learn the basic rules of professional sport.
The memoir describes the ordinary routines of life on the front line.
Parents must explain the main facts of the illness to their children.
The data reveal the full picture of how much workers are paid.
Many graduates are entering a slow job market this year.

predictions: harsh/stark/brutal before reality/truth/facts 0.4-1.0; neutral adjectives in the same frame below 0.15
notes: Card: ' harsh' x11, ' stark' x3, ' tough' x2; promotes ' reality'/' realities'.
